# cycle_dns_record (Resource)

Manages a DNS record within a Cycle DNS zone. Exactly one record type must be set under the `type` attribute, mirroring the Cycle API's record type union (A, AAAA, CNAME, NS, MX, TXT, ALIAS, SRV, CAA, or LINKED).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cycle_dns_zone" "example" {
  origin = "example.com"
  hosted = true
}

# A simple A record: www.example.com -> 203.0.113.10
resource "cycle_dns_record" "www" {
  zone_id = cycle_dns_zone.example.id
  name    = "www"

  type = {
    a = {
      ip = "203.0.113.10"
    }
  }
}

# An MX record on the zone root.
resource "cycle_dns_record" "mail" {
  zone_id = cycle_dns_zone.example.id
  name    = "@"

  type = {
    mx = {
      priority = 10
      domain   = "mail.example.com"
    }
  }
}

# A LINKED record pointing at a container, with automatic TLS.
resource "cycle_dns_record" "app" {
  zone_id = cycle_dns_zone.example.id
  name    = "app"

  type = {
    linked = {
      features = {
        tls = {
          enable = true
        }
      }

      container_id = "651586fca6078e98982dbd90"
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the record, where `@` signifies the root of the zone's origin. The Cycle API does not support renaming records, so changing this forces a new record to be created.
- `type` (Attributes) The record type. Exactly one of the nested record types must be set, mirroring the Cycle API's oneOf record union. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type))
- `zone_id` (String) The ID of the DNS zone this record belongs to. Changing this forces a new record to be created.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique ID of the DNS record.
- `resolved_domain` (String) The fully-qualified domain name resolved from the record name and the zone origin.
- `state` (String) The current state of the DNS record (e.g. `pending`, `live`).

<a id="nestedatt--type"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type`

Optional:

- `a` (Attributes) A DNS A record, mapping the name to an IPv4 address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--a))
- `aaaa` (Attributes) A DNS AAAA record, mapping the name to an IPv6 address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--aaaa))
- `alias` (Attributes) A DNS ALIAS record, returning the target domain's records at this name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--alias))
- `caa` (Attributes) A DNS CAA record, restricting which certificate authorities may issue certificates for the domain. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--caa))
- `cname` (Attributes) A DNS CNAME record, aliasing the name to another domain. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--cname))
- `linked` (Attributes) A Cycle LINKED record, pointing the name at a container, deployment, or virtual machine. Cycle manages the underlying IP mapping automatically. Exactly one of `container_id`, `deployment`, or `virtual_machine` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked))
- `mx` (Attributes) A DNS MX record for mail routing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--mx))
- `ns` (Attributes) A DNS NS record, delegating the name to a nameserver. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--ns))
- `srv` (Attributes) A DNS SRV record for service discovery. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--srv))
- `txt` (Attributes) A DNS TXT record. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--txt))

<a id="nestedatt--type--a"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.a`

Required:

- `ip` (String) The IPv4 address the A record maps to.


<a id="nestedatt--type--aaaa"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.aaaa`

Required:

- `ip` (String) The IPv6 address the AAAA record maps to.


<a id="nestedatt--type--alias"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.alias`

Required:

- `domain` (String) The domain returned from the DNS server when this alias record is requested.


<a id="nestedatt--type--caa"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.caa`

Required:

- `tag` (String) The property identifier of the record, e.g. `issue` or `issuewild`.
- `value` (String) The value associated with the tag, e.g. a certificate authority domain.


<a id="nestedatt--type--cname"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.cname`

Required:

- `domain` (String) The domain the CNAME record resolves to.


<a id="nestedatt--type--linked"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked`

Required:

- `features` (Attributes) Platform features applied to this LINKED record. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked--features))

Optional:

- `container_id` (String) The ID of the container this LINKED record points to.
- `deployment` (Attributes) Points this LINKED record at a tagged deployment within an environment. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked--deployment))
- `virtual_machine` (Attributes) Points this LINKED record at a virtual machine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked--virtual_machine))

<a id="nestedatt--type--linked--features"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked.features`

Required:

- `tls` (Attributes) TLS settings for the record. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked--features--tls))

Optional:

- `geodns` (Attributes) GeoDNS settings for the record. Defaults to disabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked--features--geodns))
- `wildcard` (Attributes) Wildcard settings for the record. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked--features--wildcard))

<a id="nestedatt--type--linked--features--tls"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked.features.tls`

Required:

- `enable` (Boolean) When `true`, Cycle automatically provisions and maintains a TLS certificate for this record.


<a id="nestedatt--type--linked--features--geodns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked.features.geodns`

Required:

- `enable` (Boolean) When `true`, Cycle attempts to route inbound requests to the geographically closest load balancer.


<a id="nestedatt--type--linked--features--wildcard"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked.features.wildcard`

Required:

- `resolve_sub_domains` (Boolean) When `true`, subdomains resolve for wildcard records. When `false`, only the primary domain resolves.



<a id="nestedatt--type--linked--deployment"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked.deployment`

Required:

- `environment_id` (String) The ID of the environment with the deployment tag mapping to reference.
- `match` (Attributes) Which container and tagged deployment this record targets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--type--linked--deployment--match))

<a id="nestedatt--type--linked--deployment--match"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked.deployment.match`

Required:

- `container` (String) The identifier of the container in the environment this record points to.

Optional:

- `tag` (String) The deployment tag this record points to. Tags are set on the environment root and map to a deployment version.



<a id="nestedatt--type--linked--virtual_machine"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.linked.virtual_machine`

Required:

- `id` (String) The ID of the virtual machine.

Optional:

- `dmz` (Boolean) When `true`, traffic to this domain skips the load balancer and goes directly to the virtual machine via the gateway service. Defaults to `false`.



<a id="nestedatt--type--mx"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.mx`

Required:

- `domain` (String) The mail server domain this MX record points to.
- `priority` (Number) The priority of this MX record; lower values are preferred.


<a id="nestedatt--type--ns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.ns`

Required:

- `domain` (String) The domain of the nameserver for this record.


<a id="nestedatt--type--srv"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.srv`

Required:

- `domain` (String) The domain providing the service.
- `port` (Number) The port number of the service.
- `priority` (Number) The priority of the record; lower values are preferred.
- `weight` (Number) The weight of the record — breaks ties for priority.


<a id="nestedatt--type--txt"></a>
### Nested Schema for `type.txt`

Required:

- `value` (String) The value of the TXT record.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# DNS records are imported via the composite ID "zone_id/record_id".
terraform import cycle_dns_record.www 651586fca6078e98982dbd90/651586fca6078e98982dbd91
```
